slides.title: The home health nurse is caring for a 26-year-old client who has pulmonary tuber
text: Question: The home health nurse is caring for a 26-year-old client who has pulmonary tuberculosis and is receiving newly prescribed streptomycin 1 gram intramuscular (IM) once daily. Which of the following actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.
A. Remind the client to monitor for hearing changes.
B. Tell the client to contact the primary health care provider if the stool is black.
C. Advise the client to take over-the-counter acetaminophen for fever and headache.
D. Inform the client that there is no need for a follow-up visit once the medication is completed.
E. Advise the client to continue streptomycin therapy before any procedures that may require anesthesia.
Correct answers: A. Remind the client to monitor for hearing changes.; C. Advise the client to take over-the-counter acetaminophen for fever and headache.
notes: • “Remind the client to monitor for hearing changes.” – Streptomycin is an aminoglycoside and can damage the 8th cranial nerve (hearing and balance).
• “Advise the client to take over-the-counter acetaminophen…” – Acetaminophen is the safer choice for fever and headache; NSAIDs add kidney risk to an aminoglycoside.
• Black stool is not an expected effect of streptomycin.
• Follow-up visits are still needed after treatment (TB therapy is long and monitored).
• Streptomycin can increase the effect of anesthesia and muscle relaxants, so the client should tell the provider rather than simply continue it before procedures.
(Answer key not on the slide; worked out with NCLEX reasoning, so check it against your class notes.) The acetaminophen option is the least certain part of this key.
